patients.summary: Healthy college biology student and barista who joined in 2023 with seasonal allergic rhinitis and acne on a combined pill, clindamycin gel and cetirizine. Last seen December 2024; in 2026 three outside ED visits for first-episode psychosis (schizophreniform disorder) and outpatient psychiatry starting aripiprazole reach the chart as records only.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20F here to establish care. Aging out of her pediatric and adolescent practice; records requested. Biology major at a local university, taking a reduced course load while she works; lives off campus with a roommate. Works part time as a barista, mostly weekend mornings.

PMH
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis since middle school. Sneezing, itchy eyes and congestion spring and fall, also worse when she dusts or changes the bedding. Was told she reacts to dust mites. Takes cetirizine 10 mg every day, which keeps it quiet.
- Acne, face, since about 15. Uses clindamycin 1% gel morning and night. On a combined pill (drospirenone 3 mg / ethinyl estradiol 0.02 mg) for a few years, started for contraception and the skin; she feels the skin is the best it has been.
PSH: tonsils out at 7. Wisdom teeth out at 18.
Allergies: penicillin (told as a child, she doesn't know what happened). Dust mites.
Meds: as above.
FH: mother with generalized anxiety. Maternal uncle has schizophrenia. Paternal grandmother with bipolar I disorder. No early heart disease or cancers she knows of.
Social: never smoked, no vaping. Alcohol socially, 1-2 drinks on weekends. No drugs. Sexually active, uses the pill.

ROS: no headaches, no leg pain or swelling, no chest pain. Periods regular and light on the pill. Mood good, sleeping fine. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well appearing, pleasant. BP and HR as charted. Nasal turbinates mildly pale, no polyps. Oropharynx clear, tonsils absent. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Skin: a few closed comedones on the forehead and chin, no cysts or scarring. Mood and affect normal.

A/P
1. Seasonal allergic rhinitis, controlled. Continue cetirizine. Dust-mite covers for the mattress and pillows discussed.
2. Acne vulgaris, mild and controlled. Continue clindamycin gel and the pill. Will take over the refills.
3. Contraception. Combined pill, normal BP, nonsmoker, no migraine with aura, no clotting history. OK to continue.
4. Health maintenance: flu and COVID in October. Pap due after she turns 21; plan at a physical next summer. Will review vaccine history when records arrive.
RTC about 6 months.

documents.title: Prior pediatric practice records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
41 pages from the patient's former pediatric and adolescent practice, covering 2008 through June 2023.

Contents: well visits yearly through age 20; immunization record (childhood series complete; Tdap, MenACWY and HPV at 11, second HPV later that year, MenACWY booster at 16); tonsillectomy in 2010 by an outside ENT, uncomplicated; allergic rhinitis managed with cetirizine; acne managed with topical clindamycin, combined oral contraceptive started 2020 by the adolescent medicine clinician; penicillin listed as an allergy since early childhood, reaction not documented. Adolescent depression screens negative each year. Dental office letter 2021 noting third molar extraction.

Immunizations entered into the chart from the record. Original filed under media.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pediatric records reviewed. Vaccines up to date except seasonal. Two-dose HPV series done before 15, so complete. Penicillin reaction never documented there either; leave as listed. Nothing else to act on.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after class for vaccines. Afebrile, feels well, no prior vaccine reactions. Allergies reviewed: penicillin, dust mites. Flu vaccine IM left deltoid. COVID 2023-24 formula IM right deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 minutes, fine, left ambulatory.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month check. Turned 21 last month. Spring semester started, heavy lab schedule this term. Skin is about the same: a few small bumps around the chin before her period, nothing painful. Using the gel twice a day most days. Pill going fine, no missed pills she can remember, no headaches, no breakthrough bleeding. Allergies quiet over the winter, still on cetirizine.

O: BP and HR as charted. Skin: scattered closed comedones on the chin, two small papules, no nodules. Rest deferred.

A/P: Acne vulgaris, mild, stable on clindamycin gel and the combined pill; no change. Contraception: normotensive on an estrogen pill, continue, refilled for a year. Seasonal allergic rhinitis, continue cetirizine. Physical with Pap this summer. RTC for the physical.

documents.title: Allergies
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My allergies are kicking in with everything blooming. Eyes itchy, sneezing on the walk to campus. I'm still taking the cetirizine every day, is it ok to keep doing that all spring or should I be taking a break from it?

documents.title: RE: Allergies
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Yolanda, yes, it's fine to take cetirizine every day through the season, no break needed. Showering and changing clothes after being outside and keeping windows closed on high-pollen days help too. If it stops working let me know and we can talk about other options.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21F for her physical. Fall semester starts in two weeks; she has two organic chemistry labs this term. Still at the coffee shop on weekends. Feels well.

Interval: no ED or urgent care visits. Skin calm over the summer. Allergies were bad for about three weeks in May, cetirizine was enough. Pill fine.

Meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily; drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol 1 tab daily; clindamycin 1% gel BID.
Allergies: penicillin (reaction unknown); dust mites.
Social: never smoker. Weekend drinks, 1-2. No drugs. Sexually active, on the pill.
Screens: PHQ-9 2 (a little tired around exams), GAD-7 3. No SI.

ROS otherwise negative: no headaches or vision change, no chest pain, no calf pain, no abdominal pain, periods light and regular.

Exam: BP, HR and BMI as charted. Alert, well groomed, conversational. HEENT: TMs clear, mild turbinate pallor. Neck no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap and NAAT swab obtained, no discharge. Skin: a few comedones on the chin. Extremities without edema. Mood and affect bright.

A/P
- Preventive: first Pap today. CT/GC NAAT. One-time HIV and hep C screening. Baseline CBC, CMP and fasting lipids. Flu and COVID in October.
- Acne, rhinitis, contraception: all stable, continue as is.
- RTC in about 4 months for a check-in, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Yolanda, all of your bloodwork from Tuesday is normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol. HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative, and the chlamydia and gonorrhea tests were negative. The Pap smear takes about a week; I'll message you when it's back.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap came back normal, no abnormal cells. At your age the next one is due in 3 years.

documents.title: RE: Pap result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thank you!

documents.body: Pt here for seasonal vaccines. Denies fever or illness today. Last year's shots: sore arm only. Flu (2024-25 trivalent) L deltoid IM, COVID 2024-25 R deltoid IM, lots and expirations logged. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Check-in between finals. Last exam is Tuesday. Busy semester with a genetics lab and more hours at the cafe, but she says she is doing well. Sleeping 6-7 hours. PHQ-2 0. Skin good, uses the gel most nights now rather than twice a day. Pill without problems. Allergies quiet since September.

O: BP and HR as charted, weight stable. Calm, organized, good eye contact, laughing about the semester. Skin: faint comedones on the chin only.

A/P
1. Contraception: normotensive, continue drospirenone/EE; 12 months sent.
2. Acne vulgaris: controlled; clindamycin gel refilled. Twice daily is the instruction but once nightly seems to be holding.
3. Seasonal allergic rhinitis: continue cetirizine as needed or daily in season.
4. HM: flu and COVID done in October. Pap 2024 normal.
Physical next August. Good luck with finals.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Regional hospital emergency department. Visit 02/10/2026, arrived 21:40.

CC: roommate concerned about odd behavior.

HPI: 23-year-old woman brought in by her roommate. For the past several weeks she has kept to her room and rarely comes out. She tells us she believes her thoughts are going out over the radio where other people can hear them, and that she hears voices that talk about what she is doing. Patient is guarded and answers briefly; roommate supplies most of the history. No prior psychiatric diagnosis or treatment. Denies drug use.

PMH: seasonal allergic rhinitis, acne.
PSH: tonsillectomy as a child; wisdom teeth extraction.
Home meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily; drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol daily; clindamycin 1% gel to face twice daily.
Allergies: penicillin; dust mites.
Family history: no family psychiatric history obtained at this visit.
Social: never smoker, alcohol on weekends, 1-2 drinks. College student, works part time at a coffee shop.

Vitals: within normal limits, see flowsheet.
Exam: Unkempt hair and clothing. Appears to be attending to internal stimuli, glancing to the side and pausing mid-answer. Alert and oriented x3. Recall intact. Speech coherent, slowed and soft. Cardiopulmonary and abdominal exams unremarkable.

Results: CBC normal. BMP normal. TSH normal. Urine toxicology negative.

Assessment: new-onset psychotic symptoms with thought broadcasting and auditory hallucinations; medical and substance causes not supported by today's workup. Schizophreniform disorder.

Disposition: discharged home in the care of her roommate. Outpatient psychiatry referral information provided. No medications started. Return for any thoughts of harming self or others or worsening symptoms.

Record received by fax 02/13/2026.

documents.body:
OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Regional hospital ED. Date of service 03/21/2026.

CC: behavior getting worse; not going to school or work.

HPI: 23F with allergic rhinitis and acne, seen here about a month ago for new psychotic symptoms. Brought back today by the same roommate. Since then she has pulled away further and is often heard talking to herself. She has told the roommate that the government put a chip in her brain. She stopped going to her classes and recently quit her coffee shop job, convinced her coworkers were in on a plan to keep watch on her. This is her first psychiatric illness; she has not connected with outpatient psychiatry.

Problems: schizophreniform disorder (this ED, 02/2026); seasonal allergic rhinitis; acne vulgaris.
PSH: tonsillectomy, wisdom teeth.
Home meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily; drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol daily; clindamycin 1% gel BID.
Allergies: penicillin; dust mites.
FH: maternal uncle with schizophrenia; paternal grandmother with bipolar I; mother with generalized anxiety disorder.
Social: never smoker; weekend alcohol 1-2 drinks.

MSE: disheveled, visibly anxious, looks away throughout. Preoccupied, mumbles under her breath while being interviewed. Speech disorganized. Expresses fixed paranoid beliefs about being monitored.

Results: urine toxicology negative.

Impression: schizophreniform disorder, worsening.
Disposition: discharged home with roommate; outpatient psychiatry referral renewed with contact numbers. No medications started.

Received by fax 03/25/2026.

documents.body:
OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Regional hospital ED, 05/23/2026.

CC: increasingly unusual behavior.

HPI: 23-year-old woman, third ED visit since February for progressive psychotic symptoms (social withdrawal, thought broadcasting, hearing voices, persecutory beliefs). Roommate brought her in. Over roughly three months she has become more isolated and mutters to herself in her room for hours. She let her work responsibilities slide and then stopped going in at all. Roommate describes laughing at odd moments and reacting to things no one else sees. It is hard to hold a conversation with her; she skips from one unrelated subject to another. She has stopped showering, and her hair and clothes are unwashed.

Problems: schizophreniform disorder; seasonal allergic rhinitis; acne vulgaris.
Home meds (as reported): cetirizine, drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol, clindamycin gel.
Allergies: penicillin; dust mites.
FH: maternal uncle schizophrenia; paternal grandmother bipolar I; mother GAD.
Social: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks on weekends.

Exam: minimal eye contact, flat affect, speech mumbled with loose associations. Neuro: cranial nerves intact, strength and sensation normal, gait steady; nonfocal.

Results: urine drug screen negative. BMP within normal limits.

Impression: schizophreniform disorder, progressive.
Disposition: discharged home with roommate. Outpatient psychiatry intake appointment arranged for early June. No medications started.

Received 05/27/2026.

documents.title: Psychiatry Initial Evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY
Initial evaluation, seen 06/09/2026.

Reason for referral: first-episode psychosis after three ED visits (February, March and May 2026).

History: 23-year-old woman, undergraduate biology student, until this winter also working part time as a barista; she has stopped attending classes. Over the past several months she has withdrawn from friends, stopped working and spends most of the day in her room. She endorses hearing voices that remark on what she does and a belief that others can hear her thoughts; she still feels she is being watched. Workup in the ED, including blood counts, chemistries, TSH and repeated urine drug screens, was unrevealing. No prior psychiatric treatment. Denies substance use; weekend alcohol only, never smoker. Lives with her roommate; her mother came to today's appointment and is involved.

Family psychiatric history: maternal uncle with schizophrenia; paternal grandmother with bipolar I disorder; mother with generalized anxiety disorder.

Medical: seasonal allergic rhinitis, acne. Meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily, drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol daily, clindamycin 1% gel. Allergies: penicillin; dust mites.

MSE: poorly groomed, limited eye contact, flat affect, speech soft with tangential stretches, perceptual disturbances endorsed, persecutory content, no suicidal or homicidal ideation, insight limited.

Diagnosis: schizophreniform disorder.

Plan:
1. Start aripiprazole 5 mg by mouth once daily. Reviewed common side effects including restlessness, and the reason for an antipsychotic. Patient and mother agree.
2. Weight and metabolic monitoring will be followed here.
3. Return in 6 weeks, sooner if worse. Crisis line numbers given.

Please contact our office with any concerns. cc: primary care physician.

documents.title: Psychiatry letter filed
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry initial evaluation letter received and filed. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY
Follow-up, seen 07/21/2026.

Yolanda returns six weeks after starting aripiprazole 5 mg daily, with her mother. Taking it every evening; her mother has been helping her keep track. Voices come less often now and bother her less when they do. No restlessness, no stiffness or tremor. Weight unchanged from the first visit.

MSE: casually dressed, better groomed than at intake, eye contact improved but still brief, affect restricted, speech more organized, no suicidal ideation.

Assessment: schizophreniform disorder, partial response to aripiprazole, tolerating well.
Plan: continue aripiprazole 5 mg daily. Return in about 6 weeks.

cc: primary care physician.

I sent 3 months of your birth control to your pharmacy tonight so you won't run out. Our front desk will reach out to set up a visit with me in the next few weeks; bring your current medicines with you.
